profiles.meeting_scenario: Three weeks into a pilot at the Longhe Power Station, a unified deep-learning object detection system for fire, smoke, water leakage, and oil leakage was integrated with the plant's existing video management system across 46 cameras. After the integration cutover, the night shift on Unit 2 began seeing a sharp increase in anomaly notifications, especially around the auxiliary pump room, even though daytime performance remained acceptable. The meeting is a troubleshooting session between the vendor's computer vision deployment lead and the plant's safety systems engineer to diagnose whether the problem is coming from the model, the video feed configuration, or the way alerts are being generated after integration. The agenda is to compare what each side believes the symptom is, review the suspect camera/feed, decide how to reproduce the issue using recent footage, and select a short-term fix before a regulator walk-through later in the week. The expected outcome is an agreed next-step test and a provisional mitigation plan for the night-shift alarm spike.

members.name: Li Wei
members.expertise: Object detection deployment, model tuning, inference optimization, video analytics integration
members.background: Li works for the external AI vendor that developed the unified anomaly detector and has led several industrial vision pilots in substations, refineries, and utility sites; he is responsible for keeping the current power-station pilot on schedule without reopening model training.
members.private_state: He wants to show that the underlying detector is still sound and that the issue can be resolved with deployment-side tuning rather than a costly retraining cycle or a delayed acceptance milestone.
hidden_assumptions: When people discuss an 'alarm' in troubleshooting, they are referring to any detector output that crosses the inference confidence threshold and appears in the analytics logs.
Plant camera labels such as 'Camera 12' refer by default to the visible-light channel unless someone explicitly says thermal or infrared.
Replaying 'last week's night footage' means using the exported diagnostic clips from the VMS share, which are sufficient to reproduce model behavior for troubleshooting.
If replay results look clean after threshold and suppression tuning, that is enough evidence that the system is stable for sign-off.

members.name: Chen Rong
members.expertise: Control-room alarm integration, CCTV operations, plant safety procedures, industrial monitoring systems
members.background: Chen is the in-house engineer responsible for keeping camera-based safety monitoring usable for operators and for ensuring any changes fit within the plant's approved alarm workflow; he knows the station's night-shift routines and camera layout in detail.
members.private_state: He wants nuisance notifications reduced quickly without changing certified operator workflows or introducing any fix that would require a broader procedural approval before the audit.
hidden_assumptions: An 'alarm' means an operator-visible alert that survives the plant's dwell/filter logic and actually appears on the control-room console with the normal notification behavior.
For dual-sensor devices at night, a location label such as 'Camera 12' naturally refers to the thermal channel operators rely on overnight unless someone explicitly says visible.
Reviewing 'last week's night footage' means using the archived continuous NVR stream at native frame rate with the same masks and alarm logic the plant actually ran.
The system is only stable once live overnight operation is quiet for operators, not merely when offline replay numbers improve.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about reducing the 'alarm count' and reviewing 'alarms' from the night shift.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means raw detector events above confidence threshold in the analytics server logs, including events that may later be filtered before reaching operators.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means only control-room-visible alerts that survive dwell time, masking, and alert aggregation and are actually experienced by operators.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In troubleshooting meetings, 'alarm' is a routine term that sounds shared and concrete, so both assume the other is using the standard operational meaning from their own layer of the system.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'Camera 12 by the auxiliary pump room' as the main problem source.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the visible-light channel associated with the dual-sensor device because that is how the vendor's deployment spreadsheet indexes the camera.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the thermal/night channel from the same physical device because that is the feed operators monitor overnight and colloquially call Camera 12.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The physical location and camera label are genuinely shared, so the reference feels precise enough that neither thinks to disambiguate the channel within the device.

misalignment_points.topic: How to 'replay last week's night footage'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'replay last week's night footage' to reproduce the issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to use the exported diagnostic clips from the VMS share, which are short event-centered segments and are typically transcoded for troubleshooting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes they will use the archived continuous NVR stream at native settings, because that preserves the actual overnight context and plant-side filtering behavior.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Replay sounds like a straightforward diagnostic step, and both are used to their own organization's default replay workflow, so the phrase falsely signals alignment on method.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means for the system to be 'stable enough to sign off'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the system 'stable enough' before tomorrow's review or sign-off discussion.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes stability means the backtest shows a materially lower detector event rate without obvious misses on sampled clips, making it acceptable to push threshold changes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes stability means operators experience a quiet live night shift with no nuisance console alerts while still trusting that true incidents would surface normally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'stable enough' is a common managerial shorthand in time-pressured troubleshooting, and each side silently fills in the validation standard they always use.
